title: Finite group covers reflect reductivity of the neutral component
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $U,V$ be affine $F$-group schemes of finite type, and let $q:U\to V$ be a group homomorphism which is finite and surjective on underlying spaces. Here finite means that $F[U]$ is a finite module over $F[V]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Group schemes over a ring have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with that ring as base. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $U$ is smooth. Let $U^0$ be the connected component of its identity, with its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $H=(V_{\mathrm{red}})^0$ be the identity component of the reduction of $V$, where reduction means quotienting coordinate rings by their nilradicals. Suppose $H$ is reductive. Over a field, reductive means smooth, geometrically connected, affine of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure; unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Then $q$ restricts to a finite surjective homomorphism $U^0\to H$, and $U^0$ is reductive. No separability or reducedness assumption on its finite kernel is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381: Proposition 4.3, first paragraph of proof (finite-kernel case of its equal-dimension unipotent-radical argument), printed p.8; elementary component restriction for a finite surjective homomorphism

proof.text: Put $G=U^0$. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $U$ and $V$. It gives closed and open identity subgroups, geometric irreducibility and finite type, and identifies $(V^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ as a smooth connected group with underlying space $|V^0|$. Reduction commutes with restriction to an open subscheme: on each affine chart both operations quotient the same local rings by their nilpotents. Hence $(V^0)_{\mathrm{red}}=H$. These subgroups are affine, since a closed subscheme of an affine scheme is an affine quotient by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], $G$ is smooth. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] it is reduced. In particular $G$ is affine, smooth, geometrically connected and of finite type, as required for reductivity.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), Tag 047R (lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect), Tags 047N and 047P; smooth restriction: morphisms, Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); reducedness: varieties, Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: The continuous image of the connected space $|G|$ is connected and contains the identity, so $q(G)\subseteq |V^0|=|H|$. Since $G$ is reduced and $H\hookrightarrow V$ is closed, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives a unique factor $f:G\to H$. It is a homomorphism: its multiplication, inverse and identity identities can be checked after the closed immersion into $V$, where they are the identities for $q$; closed immersions are injective on all test-scheme maps by the affine quotient description [def-weil-closed-immersion]. To check finiteness, write $R=F[V]$, $B=F[U]$, $F[G]=B/J$, and $F[H]=R/I$. The map $R\to B/J$ kills $I$ by this factorization. Images of any finite $R$-module generating set of $B$ generate $B/J$ over $R/I$. Thus $f$ is finite, with no flatness assertion needed yet.

source.place: Tag 01J3 (schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme); affine quotient and finite-module argument written out; closed immersions: Tag 01QO.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], the components of $U$ are finitely many translates $g_aG$ with $g_a\in U(F)$. Put $S=|f|(|G|)\subseteq |H|$. The images $q(g_aG)=q(g_a)S$ are closed in $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], and cover $|V|$ because $q$ is surjective. Each such image is connected and contains $q(g_a)$. If it meets $|H|=|V^0|$, it is contained in that connected component; moreover the $F$-point $q(g_a)$ then factors through $H$, because its image is in $H$ and its source is reduced, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme]. Thus $|H|$ is a finite union of closed sets of the form $q(g_a)S$ with $q(g_a)\in H(F)$. It is irreducible by step 1. A finite closed cover of a nonempty irreducible space has a member equal to the whole space (induct on the number of members using the definition of irreducibility). Hence $q(g_a)S=|H|$ for some $a$. Translation by $q(g_a)^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $H$, so $S=|H|$. This proves surjectivity of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component); translations and finite closed cover argument expanded by the agent; closed images: morphisms Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper).

proof.text: The affine groups $G,H$ are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $f$, obtaining $G\xrightarrow{p}I\xrightarrow{j}H$ with $p$ faithfully flat and $j$ a closed immersion. Surjectivity of $f$ implies that $j$ is surjective on spaces. Since $H$ is reduced, apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to $\mathrm{id}_H$ and $j$: there is $s:H\to I$ with $js=\mathrm{id}_H$. The affine quotient description [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $j$ a monomorphism, so $sj=\mathrm{id}_I$ as well. Therefore $j$ is an isomorphism, and $f$ is faithfully flat. For any flat surjective morphism between affine schemes, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes its coordinate map flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes that map faithfully flat. Thus the geometric faithful flatness here, and that of the factorization maps below, have the extension-of-scalars meaning required by the unipotent-image lemma.

source.place: Proposition 4.3, first paragraph, finite-kernel specialization, read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381; agent expansion using the homomorphism theorem (Milne iAG2017, Theorem 5.39, WANTED locally) and Stacks Tag 01J3. Affine flatness: morphisms Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); faithful flatness: algebra Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: Let $N\hookrightarrow G$ be any smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. It is affine and of finite type as a closed subgroup of $G$. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $f|_N$, giving $N\xrightarrow{u}J\xrightarrow{i}H$, with $u$ faithfully flat, $J$ a finite-type group scheme, and $i$ a closed immersion. All groups are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], and $J$ is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image] now hold with $A=G$, $D=H$, and the faithfully flat $f$ from step 4. That lemma says exactly that $J$ is smooth, connected and unipotent and $i(J)$ is normal in $H$. Reductivity of $H$ therefore gives $J=\{1\}$. Consequently $f|_N$ is the constant identity homomorphism as a morphism of schemes, not merely on $F$-points.

source.place: Proposition 4.3, first paragraph of proof, unipotent image killed by the reductive target; agent expansion using the two existing homomorphism and unipotent-image nodes. No later reductive-model theorem from that paragraph is used.

proof.text: Write $C=F[H]$, $D=F[G]$, and $E=F[N]$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $D\to E$ is surjective. By step 2, $D$ is a finite $C$-module, so $E$ is a finite $C$-module. Step 5 says the map $C\to E$ equals $C\xrightarrow{e_H^*}F\to E$. Therefore the same finite generating set generates $E$ as an $F$-vector space. This is where finiteness of the cover is used; there is no assertion that its kernel is reduced. Descending chains of ideals of $E$ are descending chains of subspaces in a finite-dimensional vector space, hence stabilize. Thus $E$ is Artinian. It is reduced by smoothness of $N$ and [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], with reducedness of global sections supplied by [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Tag 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra; descending-chain proof written out); smooth implies reduced: varieties Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to $E$. It identifies $E$ with a finite product of fields, one for each maximal ideal. There is at least one factor, since the identity of $N$ gives a unital $F$-algebra map $E\to F$. If there were two or more factors, the corresponding nontrivial idempotent and its complement would give two disjoint nonempty open-and-closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}E=N$, contradicting connectedness. Hence $E$ is a field. Its identity-point map $E\to F$ is then injective and is surjective since it is the identity on the structural copy of $F$. Thus $E\cong F$ over $F$, so $N$ is the trivial subgroup. Since $N$ was arbitrary, $G$ has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Together with the smoothness, affineness, finite type and geometric connectedness of step 1, this proves that $U^0=G$ is reductive. Steps 2 and 3 give the asserted finite surjective restriction. In particular the proof also covers inseparable finite kernels.
